sub_scenario.family: rehearsal load versus protected voice clarity
sub_scenario.one_line: aviation safety instructor: reject the late session; hand off coaching with the annotated script

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the simulator script and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The flight roster review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I can conduct a ten-minute preflight briefing clearly.
That is bounded and uses normal speaking volume.
It is not simulator coaching for hours.
Someone new shadowed me in the training center this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the checkride weeks into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
On 11 February, I used an annotated script for one afternoon simulator rehearsal before a 08:15 checkride.
How was your instruction at the checkride?
Direct and audible; I had not spent the evening coaching.
I prepare scenarios by annotating the simulator script with the pilot's weak points.
Can the candidate study that before the run?
Yes, it lets us reserve speech for decisions that need discussion.
I archived last cycle's notes on the flight roster and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
You gave a conference talk last year without trouble.
That was midmorning, with amplification, and no dawn checkride after it.
The schedule made it easier.
A vendor call about the simulator script ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the training center checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the checkride weeks.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the flight roster records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
On 5 May, a delayed simulator session kept me coaching emergency calls until 21:15 before a 07:30 checkride.
What did you notice the next morning?
My instructions became hoarse during the engine-failure sequence, and a colleague took the radio prompts.
I sketched next week's plan for the checkride weeks before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the simulator script updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
My sleep has been interrupted by tinnitus recently, so I recover less well from late headset work.
Does that make written scenario preparation useful?
Yes, it keeps the evening quiet.
The chief pilot says the extra evening session would show the airline how available I am.
Does availability move the checkride?
No, the candidate and examiner are confirmed for Friday.
I closed the week by updating the training center handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
Is it sensible for me to cover the delayed Thursday simulator session before Friday's 07:30 checkride?
